title: RecoverySys Online Validation Primary Sources (2026-11-05)
description: Primary authoritative reference packet for physics equations, constants, OpenRocket benchmark route, and measured flight datasets.

sources.organization: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) / National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / United States Air Force (USAF)
sources.title: U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976 (NASA-TM-X-74335 / NOAA-S/T 76-1562)
claims: Defines standard troposphere layer from sea level to 11,000 geopotential meters (H = 0 to 11,000 m')
Standard sea level temperature T0 = 288.15 K (15.0 °C)
Standard sea level pressure P0 = 101,325 Pa (1,013.25 hPa)
Standard sea level mass density rho0 = 1.2250 kg/m^3
Standard sea level acceleration of gravity g0 = 9.80665 m/s^2
Troposphere standard temperature lapse rate L = -0.0065 K/m' (-6.5 K/km)
Specific gas constant for dry air R = 287.05287 J/(kg*K) (derived from universal gas constant R* = 8314.32 J/(kmol*K) and mean molecular weight M0 = 28.9644 kg/kmol)
Ratio of specific heats gamma = 1.40 (dimensionless)
Speed of sound equation a = sqrt(gamma * R * T)
Geopotential altitude H related to geometric altitude Z via H = (r0 * Z) / (r0 + Z) where r0 = 6,356,766 m

conventions.heightReference: Geopotential altitude H vs geometric altitude Z. At 11,000 geometric meters, geopotential altitude is 10,981 m' (0.17% discrepancy). RecoverySys and typical rocketry software treat altitude as geometric without geopotential correction below 15 km.
conventions.gasConstantDiscrepancy: NASA 1976 uses R = 287.05287 J/(kg*K); RecoverySys uses R = 287.058 J/(kg*K) (0.0018% difference). Troposphere exponent (g0 / (R * L)) is 5.255877 in 1976 standard, while RecoverySys uses 5.2559.

sources.reuseConstraints: Public domain work of the United States Government. Official publication approved for public release with unlimited distribution.

sources.organization: U.S. Navy / Naval Weapons Center (NWC) China Lake & Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC)
sources.title: Parachute Recovery Systems Design Manual (NWC TP 6575 / DTIC AD-A247666)
claims: Aerodynamic parachute drag equation: Drag = 0.5 * rho * v^2 * (Cd * S)
Reference area conventions: Nominal/constructed canopy area S0 = (pi / 4) * D0^2 based on flat canopy diameter D0; projected frontal area Sp = (pi / 4) * Dp^2 based on inflated projected diameter Dp
Drag area equivalence: (Cd * S) is the invariant aerodynamic drag quantity; C_D0 is referenced to S0, while C_Dp is referenced to Sp. Typically Dp ~ 0.65 to 0.70 * D0, so C_Dp ~ 2.0 to 2.2 * C_D0
Flat circular solid canopy drag coefficient C_D0 ranges between 0.75 and 0.80 based on nominal surface area S0
Terminal descent velocity v_term = sqrt((2 * m * g) / (rho * Cd * S))
Parachute opening shock force Fo = Cx * (Cd * S) * q, where q = 0.5 * rho * v^2 and Cx is the opening-force coefficient (Pflanz method / Knacke shock factor)
Typical opening-force coefficients Cx: Flat circular ~1.6 to 1.8; Conical ~1.4 to 1.5; Cruciform ~1.1 to 1.2 (reefed/controlled) up to ~2.0+ (uncontrolled); Ringslot ~1.05 to 1.20
Snatch force kinematics: Occurs at canopy line-stretch before canopy inflation, caused by accelerating parachute mass to forebody velocity. Minimized by deployment bags and line-first staging.
Shock cord linear elastic energy capacity: Capacity_J = 0.5 * k * (Delta_L_max)^2, where k = F_rated / Delta_L_max

units.velocity: Feet per second (ft/s) and meters per second (m/s)

conventions.areaAmbiguity: Rocketry hobbyists and vendors frequently quote parachute diameter without specifying whether Cd is referenced to flat constructed area S0 or inflated projected area Sp. Using Sp-based Cd (~1.5) with flat diameter D0 overestimates drag area by ~2.2x.
conventions.openingShockCd: Knacke defines opening shock as Fo = Cx * (Cd * S) * q. RecoverySys's computeOpeningShockLoad computes force as Cx * 0.5 * rho * v^2 * S without multiplying by Cd, effectively defining Cx as a lumped shock-drag coefficient assuming Cd = 1.0.

sources.reuseConstraints: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited (Statement A). U.S. Navy technical report.

sources.organization: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Glenn Research Center
sources.title: Flight Equations with Drag (Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics)
claims: Closed-form analytical solution for vertical 1-DOF ascent coasting with quadratic drag under constant gravity and density
Coast apogee altitude equation: y_max = (Vt^2 / (2 * g)) * ln(1 + (V0^2 / Vt^2))
Coast time to apogee equation: t_apogee = (Vt / g) * arctan(V0 / Vt)
Analytical terminal velocity Vt = sqrt((2 * m * g) / (Cd * rho * A))
Provides exact, non-iterative numerical benchmark reference with zero quadrature step error

conventions.coordinateSystem: Vertical 1-DOF (+y upward, gravity downward). Drag always opposes velocity vector.
conventions.assumptions: Constant atmospheric density rho and constant vehicle drag coefficient Cd. Applicable for low-altitude coast verification where density change is negligible or bounded.

sources.reuseConstraints: Public domain work of the United States Government.

sources.organization: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Glenn Research Center
sources.title: Earth Atmosphere Equation - Metric (Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics)
claims: Confirms 11,000 meter boundary for Earth troposphere and constant -56.46 °C temperature in lower stratosphere (11-25 km)
Educational piecewise curve fits: T = 15.04 - 0.00649*h (°C), p = 101.29 * ((T + 273.1)/288.08)^5.256 (kPa)
Gas law density equation: rho = p / (0.2869 * (T + 273.1)) (kg/m^3)

conventions.conflict: Constants differ from official ISA 1976 (T0=15.04 vs 15.00, P0=101.29 vs 101.325 kPa, exponent 5.256 vs 5.255877). RecoverySys must maintain explicit distinction and not use Glenn educational fits as true ISA standard.

sources.reuseConstraints: Public domain work of the United States Government.

sources.organization: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Weather Service (NWS)
sources.title: Information About Wind Barbs
claims: Meteorological wind direction strictly indicates the direction FROM which the wind is blowing
Direction is specified on a 36-point compass (degrees clockwise from True North, 0° to 360°)
A West wind (270°) blows eastward; an East wind (90°) blows westward
Parachute drift direction is opposite to wind direction: drift_bearing = (wind_direction + 180°) mod 360°

units.direction: Degrees (°), 0 to 360 clockwise from True North
units.speed: Knots (converted to mph or m/s via standard conversion factors: 1 knot = 1.15078 mph = 0.514444 m/s)

conventions.signConvention: Cartesian wind velocity vector is [ -v * sin(theta), -v * cos(theta) ]. Inverted wind signs would cause rockets to drift upwind, a critical physical falsifier.

sources.reuseConstraints: Public domain work of the United States Government.

sources.title: OpenRocket Technical Documentation (v13.05)
claims: OpenRocket 6-DOF simulation framework and extended Barrowman aerodynamic drag model
Runge-Kutta 4th order (RK4) integration with dynamic time-stepping
Parachute model: Parachute.java implements constant drag coefficient (DEFAULT_CD = 0.8) and area getArea() = pi * (diameter / 2)^2
Streamer model: Streamer.java implements aspect-ratio and fabric-density dependent Cd (max 0.40, default 0.60)
Flight event state machine: Launch rod clearance, motor burnout, apogee, recovery device deployment, ground hit

conventions.exportFormat: CSV export via CSVExport.java exports time series with explicit SI units. Simulation summaries stored in zipped XML format (.ork).
conventions.headlessLimitation: OpenRocket mainline (through 23.09) lacks a native CLI headless mode in SwingStartup.java (checks GraphicsEnvironment.isHeadless() and exits). CLI automation requires virtual framebuffer (Xvfb), JPype scripting, or parsing saved .ork simulation runs.

sources.reuseConstraints: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA 3.0). Free software documentation.

sources.organization: OpenRocket Project / ThrustCurve.org / National Association of Rocketry (NAR)
sources.title: OpenRocket 23.09 Motor Thrust Curves Database (RASAero_Motors.eng)
claims: Certified commercial solid rocket motor thrust curves measured and published by NAR Standards & Testing (S&T)
Standard RASP .ENG format: header with designation, diameter (mm), length (mm), delays, propellant mass (kg), total mass (kg), manufacturer
Contains discrete time (s) vs thrust (N) data pairs for piecewise linear interpolation
Covers motors across classes A through M with certified total impulse and burn durations

conventions.interpolation: Piecewise linear interpolation between recorded test points. Total impulse is trapezoidal numerical integral of curve.
conventions.massDepletion: Propellant mass is assumed to deplete proportionally to cumulative delivered impulse (Tsiolkovsky mass depletion).

sources.reuseConstraints: GNU General Public License v3 / Open source rocketry database.

sources.title: Prometheus High-Power Rocket TeleMetrum Dual-Deploy Flight Telemetry (2022-06-24)
claims: First-party measured dual-deploy rocketry flight recorded at 100 Hz by commercial COTS avionics (Altus Metrum TeleMetrum v6, serial 5115)

Full flight envelope: Boost (t=-0.3 to 4.96 s), Coast (t=4.96 to 29.93 s), Drogue deploy at apogee (t=29.93 s, altitude 3,888.7 m AGL), Main deploy (t=157.97 s, altitude 448.9 m AGL), Touchdown (t=237.94 s)
Peak apogee: 3,903.8 m AGL (12,807.6 ft)
Peak speed: 317.9 m/s (1,042.9 ft/s, Mach 0.93)
Observed drogue descent rate: 26.9 m/s (88.2 ft/s) over 128.0 s duration
Observed main descent rate: 5.61 m/s (18.4 ft/s) over 79.97 s duration
Observed GPS pad position: 32.9395046° N, -106.9114515° W (Spaceport America, NM)
Observed GPS landing position: 32.9494937° N, -106.9154488° W
Observed total ground drift: 1,171.7 m (3,844.1 ft) at bearing 341.4° (NNW)

conventions.sensorUncertainty: Barometric pressure sensor resolution +/- 1 Pa (~0.1 m near ground, ~0.8 m near 4000 m). Sensor sampling at 100 Hz subjected to pyrotechnic bay pressurization spikes during drogue and main deployment charges. GPS horizontal position error ~2.5 m CEP (HDOP < 2.0).

sources.reuseConstraints: MIT License. Publicly available open-source research dataset.

sources.organization: Projeto Jupiter (Universidade de São Paulo) / RocketPy Team
sources.title: Juno III Spaceport America Cup 2023 Measured Flight Dataset
claims: First-party measured flight data from Spaceport America Cup 2023 (10k Solid SRAD category, June 23, 2023)
Registered flight card apogee: 3,213 m
COTS barometric altimeter (Missile Works RRC3 Sport) and COTS GNSS logged simultaneously
Real-world recovery failure mode: Main parachute failed to deploy; drogue descent continued from apogee (3,116 m) all the way to ground impact
Captures authentic recovery event pressure pulse: avionics bay pressure abruptly spikes from 580 hPa to 191 hPa transient during ejection charge before stabilizing

conventions.sensorUncertainty: RRC3 barometric altitude calculated via standard atmosphere formula; barometric lag and transonic port pressure anomalies present during boost; ejection charge gas ingress alters barometric pressure reading for ~0.2 s.
